title: Continuity of solutions to abstract linear control systems
abstract: Formalization of all the numbered statements of F. Marbach, "Continuity of solutions to abstract linear control systems" (2026), https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00022. For abstract linear control systems in the sense of Weiss (a strongly continuous semigroup T on a Banach space X and bounded input maps Phi_t : L^p(R_+; U) -> X satisfying the concatenation identity), the main results are: for p = infinity, every system is zero-class, i.e. the operator norm of Phi_t tends to zero as t -> 0+ (Theorem 1.5), and t -> Phi_t u is continuous on [0, infinity) for every u in L^infinity (Corollary 1.6), a positive answer to Weiss' 1989 Problem 2.4. No integral representation of the input maps is assumed. The proof packs nearly extremal controls into one bounded operator on l^infinity and uses Phillips' lemma (Lemma 2.2), which is proved here. The development also covers the continuity of semigroup orbits (Proposition 1.2), the classical case p < infinity (Proposition 1.3), and the examples of Section 3: a non zero-class system for p < infinity (Proposition 3.1), an exotic invariant mean on periodic L^infinity functions (Lemma 3.2), and a scalar system with p = infinity without integral representation and not E_F-admissible for any Young function F (Proposition 3.3).
